title: We Can Stop Trump’s Concentration Camps
author: Barbara G. Ellis
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/paris-bilal-
bHmf5Qdkm8E-unsplash-680x383.jpg)

Image by Paris Bilal.

Nearly [70,000](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/trumps-45-billion-
expansion-immigrant-%20detention-faces-pushback-from-communities) —men, women,
and children (including newborns)—have been locked up so far in 212 federal
facilities (warehouses, private prisons, public jails, tents) in 47 states as
suspected illegal immigrants until proved innocent. A Reuters’ investigation
just reported that 400 federal judges ruled [4,421
detentions](https://www.commondreams.org/news/ice-illrgal-arrests) by ICE
(Immigration & Customs Enforcement) in the last five months were illegal. Not
only that, but [73.6 percent](https://traceports.org/immigration/quickfacts/)
of those detained had no criminal records.

For thousands of others awaiting a court’s decision—[four million immigration
cases](https://www.texastribune.org/2026/02/19/ice-detention-deaths-texas-
east-montana) are on dockets—incarceration is averaging at least [six
months](https://www.commondreams.org/opinion/trump-mass-detention-system).
Indeed, [20,200 detainees](https://www.commondreams.org/news/ice-illrgal-
arrests) have filed  _habeas corpus_ petitions that they are being held
without a “speedy” public trial and an “impartial” jury, violations of the
Constitution’s Sixth Amendment. Yet even _after_ a judge has ordered a
release, the Trump regime may ignore it. One district judge in January tracked
100 release orders that ICE had violated.

Political cynics presumably suspect Trump of deliberately swamping the
nation’s courts with his demand that ICE detain at least [3,000 suspects per
day](https://www.theguardian.com/us-newa/may/trump-ice-arrest-quota).
Moreover, his Big Beautiful Bill Act allots $38.3 billion of our taxes for
_permanent expansion_ of his [“Detention Re-engineering
Initiative.”](https://www.wsws.org/en/articles/2026/02/16/) Some regional
centers are to hold “1,000 to 1,500,” and for large-scale facilities, “7,000
to 10,000,” according to an ICE memo obtained by _Wired_ earlier this month.

The appropriation specifies a need of [135,000
beds](https://www.commondreams.org/opinion/trump-mass-detention-system) for
this “initiative” up to FY 2029. That means significant profits for
construction and the remodeling industries, not to mention private prison
companies like GEO Group, which last year earned [$254
million](https://www.commondreams.org/news/geo-group-ice-profits) of our tax
dollars, usually providing  _minimal_ services to detainees: food, clothing,
shelter, and basic medical care. The less that industry spends, however, the
greater its profits.

Currently, the Trump administration is focused on acquiring, constructing, or
leasing sites for these facilities. [Homeland Security
agents](https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/?ik) may target community leaders
desperate for any new industry to increase municipal tax revenues and “good-
paying jobs,” according to [San Antonio’s U.S. Rep. Tony
Gonzales,](https://www.texastribune.org/2026/02/19/ice-detention-deaths-texas-
east-montana) about his city.

If Trump is successful, it will also bring timeless notoriety and shame upon
this country, as did Hitler’s camps such as Auschwitz, Buchenwald, and Dachau
from the 1930s to World War II’s end in 1945.

Now, to stop Trump’s concentration camps, several towns and cities are setting
examples for others to follow when “visitors” from Homeland Security or ICE
come calling at city halls around the nation for campsites. So are individuals
unable to emulate Minneapolis’ anti-ICE demonstrators amid blizzard, subzero
temperatures, and tear gas. But individual citizens can write anti-Trump
letters or emails. Or call the White House or local Congressional
representatives to vigorously voice objections. Or sign petitions against such
camps to judges, bar associations, and protective organizations such as
Indivisible, the ACLU (American Civil Liberties Union), Moveon, and the like.

[Officials and angry residents of small and mid-sized cities are already
fighting and stopping Trump’s plans](https://www.commondreams.org/news/list-
of-ice-detention-centers) . Sometimes it’s with special elections, petitions,
ballot referendums, monumental taxes to property owners willing to rent
property for concentration camps. But often it’s by “throwing sand into his
gears” by fees, fines, and ordinances, according to Portland OR’s [city
council president](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/02/16/cities-trump-
immigration-laws-ordinances).

Such movers and shakers know the limits of water, sewer, utility, and garbage
systems and would be overwhelmed by 1,000-15,000 detainees, or 8,000 in a town
of 8,500. Too, there will be spikes in health and hospital needs for aging and
ailing detainees, or addiction withdrawals, childbirth, epidemics, and those
brutalized by sadistic guards.

For instance, negative responses to the camps came from packed town halls in
[Surprise, KS, Shakopee, MN](https://www.commondreams.org/opinion/trump-mass-
detention-system), and [Hanover, VA](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-
news/trumps-45-billion-expansion-immigrant-%20detention-faces-pushback-from-
communities) . Portland, OR’s city council created an extraordinary [Municipal
Impact Fee](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/02/16/cities-trump-immigration-
laws-ordinances) on an ICE building lease.
[Others,](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/trumps-45-billion-expansion-
immigrant-%20detention-faces-pushback-from-communities) like Democratic
majorities in some legislatures, voted outright to ban camps. Some were
imaginative, like the mayors of Oklahoma City and Salt Lake City, adjusting
building permits and leaning on landowners not to sell or rent property to DHS
or ICE. Kansas City, MO’s city council is weighing a proposal for a five-year
moratorium on building permits for federal facilities. U.S. House member Pat
Ryan (D-NY) reported [that 25,000 people signed a
petition](https://www.commondreams.org/news/list-of-ice-detention-centers)
opposing the use of a warehouse in his district. And California’s legislature
is mulling [a 50 percent tax measure](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-
news/trumps-45-billion-expansion-immigrant-%20detention-faces-pushback-from-
communities) on private prisons’ profits so hopefully they’ll look elsewhere
for campsites. Congress also has the power of the purse to stop payment on
Trump’s neo-Nazi ambitions.

At bottom, his legions of lawyers are no match for the inventive, nimble, and
knowledgeable minds of veteran legislators—and us. Taken
collectively—especially individual actions of “we the people”—we have the
power to close existing camps and new ones on Trump’s hideous list.

For those despairing and disheartened by his frightening future, it’s time for
ordinary and outraged Americans to rise from the kitchen table or TV, and do
something, anything, large or small, to stop these camps. As [advised
centuries ago](file://localhost/The%20Bible/%2013,12) :

“The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the
darkness, and let us put on the armour of light.”
